Explanation for Self-Assessment of Japanese Language Skills 
 
 
Ryukoku University launches the Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP) for international exchange students 
in the 2026 Academic Year.  
 
The goal of this program is to take advantage of the benefits of living in Japan in order to ① Gain a variety of 
experiences both within and outside of Ryukoku University and ② Improve one’s Japanese language skills 
and gain insights into the societies and cultures of various countries through interactions with Japanese students 
and other international students.  
 
To achieve this, the program incorporates project -based learning in Japanese classes, such as through 
interviews and surveys. It also makes use of Japan’s social and cultural settings – especially the unique location 
of Kyoto – by including activities such as the observation of festivals and other traditional events. 
 
 
< Class Example (JSP-B Class) > 
Topic Objectives Activities 
Travel and 
Transportation 
When presenting about one’s country and 
hometown, if there is adequate preparation 
ahead of time, can provide a somewhat 
detailed introduction about famous places, 
famous items, etc. 
・Learn vocabulary and expressions to explain  
one’s hometown and to explain both one’s 
town and the places one has been 
・Make a poster to introduce one’s hometown 
Emergency 
Situations 
In the case of an accident or disaster, can  
understand an explanation or instructions if 
the speaker’s accent is sharp. 
・Read an evacuation drill notice for information.  
Know important details at the time of evacuation 
・Visit the Kyoto City Disaster Prevention  
Center and listen to the explanation and 
instructions 
 
Student Life Understands how school circumstances 
differ according to country and region and 
is able to express (to some extent) one’s 
own opinions in detail. 
・Through texts, gain an understanding of  
education in Japan 
・Read a pamphlet of Ryukoku University- 
affiliated Heian Junior/Senior High School and 
understand the contents 
・Visit Ryukoku University-affiliated Heian  
Junior/Senior High School to observe a class 
and have a discussion with the instructors 
・Give a presentation on one’s findings from the  
visit 
 
Different 
Cultures 
With enough prior preparation, can provide 
a somewhat detailed speech about the 
differences between Japan and one’s home 
country, as well as Japan’s surprising 
aspects. 
・Attend the Gion Festival and watch the  
procession of Yamahoko floats 
・Conduct an interview in the Fushimi  
Momoyama shopping arcade 
・Provide a five-minute speech on the theme of  
cultural differences

Furthermore, with the aim of broadening students’ practical Japanese language skills, objectives are set and 
class activities are carried out by using the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) “Can Do” 
system as a reference. Using this standardized  system, the students’ home university Japanese language 
instructors and other related individuals can share Japanese language learning progress information more easily. 
In addition, our curriculum is composed of designated classes which align with the  CEFR levels. Students in 
higher-level classes are eligible to enroll in regular undergraduate or graduate-level subjects. 
 
< Organization of Classes > 
 
Japanese Classes in the Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP) are organized into four levels (JSP-Ⅱ ~ JSP-Ⅴ) 
which adhere to the CEFR framework. For each skill (Listening, Reading, Interaction, Speaking, Writing), 
learning objectives are set using “Can-Do” statements. The table below shows provides an overview of the 
“Can-Do” objectives for each class. 
 
Can-Do Objective Examples (by Class) 
Class Target 
Level 
Can-Do Objectives 
JSP-Ⅴ 
B2.2 
The student Is able to use the language fluently, accurately, and effectively on a 
wide range of subjects. Communication is natural, using correct grammar and a 
level of politeness appropriate for the situation. Interviews are carried out 
smoothly and effectively, with questions adjusted to fit the other party and an 
ability to draw out topics of great interest to the interviewee. The student is then 
able to write an article by summarizing the contents, selecting important points 
and including supplemental facts. The student absorbs numerous points of view 
in order to gain a broader understanding of Japanese culture, one’s own culture, 
and the home culture of other international students. 
B2.1 
The student is able to converse fluently and naturally, emphasizing points which 
are important to oneself and explaining related points in detail. The student is 
assertive in firmly explaining the basis of his/her own perspective. Regarding 
his/her field of interest, is able to integrate many pieces of information from 
their source and present them as grounds for an argument. In an interview, asks 
questions relevant to the other party and can draw out various topics of interest. 
Can gather the main points and compose an article with the reader in mind. 
Absorbs numerous points of view in order to gain a broader understanding of 
Japanese culture, one’s own culture, and the home culture of other students. 
 
B1.2 
When conducting a questionnaire, the student puts together results and is able to 
provide a simple presentation using graphs and data. Can put together a short 
article and speech and can state one’s opinion. Is also able to answer detailed 
questions.  Can find the information needed from a variety of informational 
sites, etc.. Is able to conduct an easy interview while confirming information 
and asking related questions, and can combine the results and compose an 
article.

JSP-Ⅳ B1.1 
With preparation, is able to give a detailed presentation. Can converse concretely 
on topics of interest. Is able to read and understand short and easy sentences. 
Can write short sentences about familiar content and topics of interest. Is able to 
understand and respect both similarities and differences between one’s own 
culture, that of Japan, and that of other countries. 
JSP-Ⅲ A2.2 
Can understand regularly used sentences and expressions regarding topics 
directly related to oneself such as personal information, family information, 
shopping, one’s neighborhood and work, etc. Can exchange information about 
short and regular, everyday matters. Can explain, in easy words, necessary 
information about one’s background and daily circumstances. 
JSP-Ⅱ A2.1 
On short and familiar topics, can attain limited information by reading and 
listening. Can make a simple presentation and write a report with short 
sentences. Can converse and answer questions on simple, everyday topics. 
 
Class placement is determined comprehensively based on the results of the “Self -Assessment of Japanese 
Language Proficiency” and the “SPOT Test.
